title: Can the Werfen GEM Hemochron 100 activated clotting time be used to monitor anticoagulation in prolonged baseline activated partial thromboplastin time?
official: Evaluation of the Werfen GEM Hemochron 100 activated clotting time point of care device in the therapeutic monitoring of unfractionated heparin in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass with a prolonged baseline activated partial thromboplastin time
summary:
Background and study aims 
During open heart surgery, patients are given a blood thinner (heparin).  Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is a blood test performed before open heart surgery to see what method should be used to monitor the heparin.  The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect a prolonged aPTT has on the different tests available to monitor heparin in patients undergoing open heart surgery who have a prolonged aPTT.  Current standard care is to monitor the heparin in these patients using a test carried out in a laboratory in another area of the hospital.  This research is to evaluate a test (the GEM Hemochron 100 ACT) that can be used within the operating theatre, removing the need to transport the blood samples to the laboratory, meaning results are available more quickly.

Who can participate?
Patients aged over 18 years with a prolonged baseline clotting time, who are undergoing open heart surgery or attending for a Haematology clinic appointment

What does the study involve?
Participants will have a drop of blood taken from their finger tip to measure their baseline clotting test on the GH100 ACT analyser. Some blood will then be taken from their arm and separated into three tubes, each containing a different amount of anticoagulant. These samples will then have tests performed on them to measure the amount of anticoagulant in them, and they will have clotting times performed on them to measure the affect the anticoagulant has on the clotting tests. Those patients undergoing open heart surgery will have blood samples taken every 30 minutes during surgery and the same tests will be performed on these blood sample. The results from before and during surgery will then be compared to one another, and the amount of anticoagulant given to patients will also be studied.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
By taking part in this study, participants will be contributing to developing a protocol for the safe management of heparin in patients with prolonged baseline clotting tests undergoing heart surgery. 
As we are taking a blood sample from a participants fingertip, it may feel a bit bruised or sore for a day or so after.  There may also be a slight bruise from the where the blood was taken from their arm.  There are no further risks and participants will always be given standard care as a minimum.

Where is the study run from? 
Lancashire Cardiac Centre and Lancashire Haematology Centre, Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
September 2026 to September 2027

Who is funding the study? 
The National School of Healthcare Science, NHS England (UK) is funding the study and Werfen (Spain) are providing the GH100 analyser

Who is the main contact? 
Claire Rowlandson, claire.rowlandson@nhs.net

interventions.name: This is a case-control study, utilising and control group of participants and a study group formed from two subgroups, A and B. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 18 years or over
2. Capacity to give informed consent
3. Prolonged aPTT (study group only)
4. Not on anticoagulant therapy at the time the baseline activated clotting time (ACT) is taken
5. Undergoing open heart surgery using a heart and lung machine (subgroup A and control group)
6. Attending a Haematology Diagnostic clinic for the investigation of a prolonged aPTT (subgroup B)
7. Normal coagulation screen (control group only)
8. Do not require a translator
Exclusion criteria:
1. Under the age of 18 years
2. Does not have capacity to give informed consent
3. Taking anticoagulant therapy at the time of baseline ACT
4. Patients with prolonged aPTT who are not having open heart surgery or attending a Haematology Diagnostic clinic
5. Participants who require a translator
